function: above_phy: FL-trained DNN for secure multicast routing; p. 15: "predicts whether the next node in the routing path is secure or not"
notes: Title and DOI checked on p. 1. The only learned component is a fully connected DNN (three hidden layers of 128 ReLU) trained by FL with weighted averaging at the CPU (eq. 25, p. 14) to reproduce the targets of the conventional blockchain-based secure routing (Fig. 11, p. 14). Its inputs are packet and block identifiers (SCID, RCID, BCMID, UType, Type, SID, DID, BRID, Dseq, Hop) and its 4 outputs are legitimate/illegitimate cluster member and secure/unsecure next node (Fig. 13 and Table IV, p. 15): a routing decision at the network layer. The abstract (p. 1) and contribution 5 (p. 3) say the FL framework also predicts the STAR-RIS configuration and phase shifts, but the DNN as specified has no such output: the phase shifts come from optimization problem (19) (p. 10: "CHc optimizes the phase shift at F-STAR-RIS to maximize the capacity of the next node"), solved with the IOPT convex solver (Table VII, p. 16), so no physical-layer decision is learned jointly with the routing one. All results are NS-3 network metrics (PDR, control overhead, routing delay, trusted nodes, execution time, energy; p. 16) against MAODV-based routing protocols (Table VIII, p. 18). no_learning was considered first, but learning is central to the method and acts on routing, which is what above_phy describes. The FL aggregation is digital at the CPU over links assumed perfect (p. 7), not over the air, so area 7 would not apply either.
